reason: The cited evidence shows DSC used for HEA melting (E1) and neutron imaging for observing melting and remixing in CoCrCuNi (E2, E3, E4), but no evidence supports the integration of these techniques, their temporal synchronization, or the claimed accuracy of the combined method. The premises about correlation and cross-validation are unsupported by prior work.
premises: DSC can measure melting temperature and enthalpy of fusion for HEAs with ±5 °C and ±5% accuracy
Cold-neutron imaging can capture spatial evolution of melting and volume changes in HEAs
DSC and neutron imaging can be temporally synchronized during rapid temperature ramps
Correlating DSC and imaging data enables extraction of entropy and liquid-phase properties
The integrated method provides cross-validated thermodynamic data across diverse HEA regions
